To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the Trp328 residue in the third transmembranous domain of GABA receptor channels is essential for pentobarbital modulation, and that the mode of pentobarbital action on the GABA receptor channel is distinct from the GABA-dependent gating process.

the barbiturate sensitivity of the GABA receptor channel is conferred by the hydrophobicity of a single residue within its third transmembrane helix, and that barbiturate modulation of the GABA-activated channel is more sensitive to the GABA concentration in homooligomeres than in heterooligomeres.

a single hydrophobic amino acid residue confers barbital sensitivity to the GABA(C) receptor channel and that this residue is located within the transmembrane domain, not within the agonist-binding domain.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular basis of pentobarbital modulation of GABA receptors, and our results suggest that Trp328 is an important determinant of barbiturate sensitivity.

the molecular mechanisms of barbiturate modulation of the GABA type C receptor, a ligand-gated chloride channel that is expressed throughout the brain and has been linked to the control of sleep and epilepsy.
the structural basis of the pentobarbital modulation of GABAA receptors and provides a new model for the design of novel anesthetic agents.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
Trp328 is the first identified barbiturate binding site within a ligand-gated channel.
the Trp328 residue in the third transmemembrane domain is the key residue that confers barbituratesensitivity to GABA type C receptor channels.
Trp328 plays an important and unique role in the function of homooligommeric GABA receptors.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Trp328 residue in the third transmembranal domain is a key determinant of barbiturate sensitivity in the GABA receptor channel.

the Trp328 residue in the third transmembrain domain is an important determinant of barbiturate sensitivity, which can be imparted to the GABA receptor channel by a simple amino acid substitution, and that the GABA and barbiturate activation domains are functionally interconnected.
the Trp residue at position 3 in the third transmembranous domain is an important determinant for the barbiturate sensitivity of the human rho1 GABA receptor channel.
The main takeaway from our work is that
a single amino acid can confer barbiturate sensitivity on a receptor that is otherwise not sensitive.
a single amino acid residue can confer barbiturate modulation to a GABA channel.
the barbiturate site on GABA receptors is located within the M3 transmembrane domain and is highly sensitive to hydrophobic residues.
